name: Sikkuth
title: Assyrian idol worshipped by Israel
summary: Sikkuth (also known as Sakkuth) was an Assyrian-Babylonian idol, likely a star god, whom the Israelites worshipped during their time in the wilderness and in the divided kingdom. The prophet Amos condemned Israel's worship of Sikkuth as an expression of their apostasy from the Lord. The name is linked to the Mesopotamian god Sakkuth (Saturn/Ninurta), and this idolatry was used as grounds for God's judgment against Israel.

keyEvents.title: Amos' condemnation of idolatry
keyEvents.description: The prophet Amos rebuked the Israelites for carrying Sikkuth as their king and Kijun as their star god, demonstrating their deep apostasy from the true God.

keyEvents.title: Amos' warning about exile
keyEvents.description: As a consequence of their idolatry, including the worship of Sikkuth, Amos warned that God would send the people into exile beyond Damascus.

keyEvents.title: The context of false worship
keyEvents.description: Amos criticized Israel's religious practice as hypocritical—they held festivals and offered sacrifices to the Lord, yet simultaneously worshipped foreign gods like Sikkuth.

keyEvents.title: Stephen's speech in Acts
keyEvents.description: Stephen quoted Amos' words about Sikkuth (the tent of Moloch) in his address to the high council, accusing the Israelites of repeated idolatry throughout history.
